title: A Record Older Than Him: Josh Kerr Smashes 27-Year-Old Mile Mark!
summary: Imagine running a whole mile faster than anyone ever has—faster than a record that stood for 27 years! That's what Josh Kerr did on Saturday in London. He ran a mile in 3 minutes and 42.66 seconds. That's about the time it takes to microwave a bag of popcorn, but he ran four whole laps around a track! The old record was set by Hicham El Guerrouj in 1999, when Kerr was just one year old. Kerr said the race was "very overwhelming" because there was so much excitement. He trained really hard for this, even taking 222-second ice baths to help his body recover. That's almost 4 minutes of freezing cold! His training partner and another runner helped set the pace perfectly. In the last 200 meters, Kerr turned on the speed and left the other runner behind. The crowd of 60,000 people at the London Stadium—built for the 2012 Olympics—cheered so loudly that Kerr said he couldn't hear anything in the final stretch. "I was deaf in the last 110 meters!" he said. Kerr is now the sixth British runner to hold the world record for the mile. He joins legends like Roger Bannister, who was the first to run a mile in under 4 minutes back in 1954. Kerr said he wants to leave his mark on the sport like those heroes. After the race, World Athletics President Sebastian Coe gave him a $50,000 check and a book about famous milers. What a day!
why_it_matters: This shows that with hard work and dedication, even records that seem impossible can be broken, inspiring you to chase your own goals in sports or school.

background_read: Before 1954, many people thought humans couldn't run a mile in under four minutes. Roger Bannister proved them wrong, and his record inspired generations of runners.
The mile world record has been held by legendary athletes like Hicham El Guerrouj (the previous record holder from Morocco), and now Josh Kerr joins that list.
London Stadium, where Kerr broke the record, was built for the 2012 Olympics and has hosted many great track and field moments.
Article_Structure: WHO: Josh Kerr, a British runner who became the sixth British miler to hold the world record.
WHAT: He ran a mile in 3 minutes and 42.66 seconds, breaking a 27-year-old record.
WHERE: At London Stadium, a venue built for the 2012 Olympics, in front of 60,000 fans.
WHY: He trained intensely with ice baths and pacing, wanting to join legends like Roger Bannister and leave a mark on the sport.

perspectives.description: He felt overwhelmed with joy and proud to achieve his dream, having trained incredibly hard with ice baths and a perfect pace strategy.
